title: Filtered cover core assertion transfer
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $X$ a reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] separated finite-type $k$-curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], $j:U\to X$ an open immersion, $r$ a prime, $R=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbb Z/r\mathbb Z)$, and $G$ a finite locally constant $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] on $U$. Let $v:V\to U$ be finite etale. Suppose $v^*G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] has a specified finite filtration $W_0=0$, $W_n\cong v^*G$, with monic inclusions $W_i\to W_{i+1}$ for $i<n$ and each cokernel the constant $R$-module sheaf $R$ on $V$. Assume all eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] for extension by zero of constant $R$ from every open in every reduced separated finite-type $k$-curve of dimension at most one. Then all eight assertions hold for $j_!(v_*v^*G)$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Apply Zariski main theorem to j composed with v and replace the finite compactification by the reduced closure of V. Etale over reduced implies V reduced, so V remains a dense open in the reduced compactification Y. Finiteness gives the separated finite-type curve structure and the dimension bound by integral incomparability. The inclusion V -> p^{-1}(U) is finite by permanence over a separated scheme; hence its dense open image is closed and is all of p^{-1}(U). A surjective open immersion is an isomorphism, giving the cartesian square.

The constant-case hypothesis gives assertions for j'_! R on Y. Exact extension by zero and short-exact devissage inductively establish them for the finite filtration, beginning with the zero object, and the terminal isomorphism gives them for j'_! v^*G. Finite pushforward and its exchange with extension by zero identify the resulting sheaf with j_! v_*v^*G.

proof_origin: Stacks 03SD: compactify the supplied finite etale cover, apply the constant-case hypothesis and filtration devissage, then finite pushforward and finite-open exchange; no retract descent is performed.
